role_title: AI Solutions Engineer, Field Engineering (synthetic fixture)
role_level: Junior-to-mid IC (roughly 1–4 years of professional work; sweet spot roughly 1–2 years, ideally at a startup)
role_summary: This person is the technical arm of sales for enterprise engineering customers: they join customer calls and explain what the platform can do with the customer's models and data, then run the customer's workload on the platform through its API, wire up endpoints, and report the numbers. The rest of the week is turning results into reports, security questionnaires, and sales material, keeping the integration guides current, and owning last-mile delivery. The screen is literal: given five models and a dataset, they should know how to benchmark them and write up a report, and present it well.

engagement_context.engagement_description: Field-engineering hires who own the pre-sales and benchmarking load for enterprise customers evaluating an inference and evaluation platform — running customer models over customer data, reporting the numbers, and being the technical voice on sales calls.
engagement_context.talent_bar_statement: Outreach-worthy here means a junior-to-mid individual contributor who already sits in customer conversations as the technical person and is hands-on enough in Python and with model APIs to benchmark several models on a dataset and write the results up.

capability_areas.name: Customer-facing technical engagement (pre-sales / solutions)
capability_areas.description: Being the technical voice in front of a customer: discovery calls with technical buyers, scoping what the product can do for their problem, demos, proofs of concept, and carrying the technical thread from first call through delivery.
builder_signals: runs the technical track of a sales cycle — discovery call, scoping, demo, POC success criteria
builds the demo or prototype that goes in front of the customer rather than presenting someone else's
writes the scoping document or technical proposal the customer's engineers sign off on
owns a POC end to end and is accountable for whether it converts
handles objections and questionnaires from technical buyers directly
user_signals: attends customer calls as a note-taker or support resource while another engineer owns the technical answer
presents decks and benchmark results produced by another team
handles ticket-based support after the sale with no pre-sale or scoping involvement
quota-carrying selling with the technical content supplied by someone else

capability_areas.name: Hands-on Python and LLM / model-API work
capability_areas.description: Writing real code day to day — Python scripts and notebooks, calling model APIs, wiring endpoints, and moving data through pipelines and internal data platforms.
builder_signals: wires up model API endpoints and runs inference across a dataset
writes Python to move, reshape, and sample data rather than only querying it
builds small services, scaffolds, or scripts that actually run in front of a customer
integrates an LLM into a pipeline, including prompt handling and output parsing
user_signals: uses a vendor UI or no-code tool to produce outputs
describes LLM work only as 'used ChatGPT/Copilot' in day-to-day productivity terms
SQL and dashboarding with no code artifact beyond queries

capability_areas.name: Model benchmarking, comparison, and reporting
capability_areas.description: Running several models over a dataset, scoring them, and turning the numbers into something a customer reads — a report, a deck, a filled-in questionnaire, a sliced data subset. A plus signal for this seat, not a gate.
builder_signals: runs a comparison across multiple models on the same dataset and reports the spread
designs the scoring or judging approach, including LLM-as-judge setups
produces the written artifact — report, write-up, client-facing summary — from the numbers they generated
slices datasets by difficulty or quality and defends the selection
user_signals: cites public leaderboard numbers without having run anything
consumes an evaluation harness someone else built to check a single model
reports metrics from an off-the-shelf monitoring dashboard

capability_areas.name: Scrappy startup delivery and written communication
capability_areas.description: Operating without a playbook: picking up the integration guide, the security questionnaire, the docs update, and the delivery packaging because someone has to, and writing clearly enough that a technical customer accepts the document.
builder_signals: wore several hats at an early-stage company — delivery, support, docs, and customer calls in one seat
authored customer-facing documentation, write-ups, or published analyses
owned a recurring deliverable with an external deadline
presented work live to an external audience
user_signals: worked narrowly inside one defined function in a large organization with handoffs on either side
contributed sections to documents owned by others

depth_distinction.builder_definition: Owning the technical thread with a customer: they are the person who runs the benchmark or builds the demo, produces the numbers or the artifact, writes the report or scoping document, and stands in front of the customer to defend it. The verbs are run, wire up, build, slice, write up, present, deliver — and the artifacts are demos, POCs, benchmark reports, scoping documents, delivered datasets or integrations.
depth_distinction.user_definition: Consuming customer-facing technical work that someone else owns: showing up on calls to support an engineer who answers the technical questions, presenting results or decks produced by another team, or building internal components that a separate solutions or sales function packages and takes to the customer. The resume language can look identical — 'worked with customers', 'supported POCs' — but the artifact was produced and defended by someone else.
depth_distinction.edge_case_guidance: Establish BUILDER from a named artifact or a first-person account of the loop — a demo they built, a POC they ran, a benchmark or analysis they produced and reported, a customer document they authored. Establish USER when the profile positively describes a supporting or downstream posture — handing off to a solutions team, presenting another team's output, post-sale ticket handling only. A title whose purpose is customer-facing technical work (solutions engineer, forward-deployed engineer, sales engineer, customer engineer at an AI or data company) supports a BUILDER read even when the profile text is thin. If a full read turns up no named artifact and no supporting-posture language, the verdict is UNKNOWN, never USER.

transferable_fundamentals_bar: A candidate without a canonical pre-sales or solutions title can still qualify: the brief explicitly invites data science, AI engineering, and analytics backgrounds that pivoted into AI. What they need to show is (1) substantial client, customer, demo, pilot, or POC work — consulting engagements, professional services, client delivery, or a data-science seat whose output went to external clients — and (2) hands-on code: Python plus work with LLMs, model APIs, or ML/data pipelines. Evaluation or benchmarking work strengthens the case and its absence never weakens it.

non_fit_patterns.label: Research scientist / research engineer
non_fit_patterns.description: Publishes, trains or post-trains models, designs benchmarks and methods as research output; career is organized around research contributions.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: This seat does not need a research engineer: a serious researcher would be wasted in an administratively necessary, customer-facing role.
examples: research engineer on a post-training team publishing eval methodology
PhD-to-research-scientist track at an AI lab
applied research scientist whose output is papers and internal model work

non_fit_patterns.label: Backend / infra / platform / ML engineer with no customer contact
non_fit_patterns.description: Builds services, pipelines, training infrastructure, or platform components entirely behind an internal interface.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Hands-on code is only one of the three gates; this seat lives on customer calls and owns the technical conversation, and nothing in this trajectory shows that work.
examples: backend engineer on a payments service
ML platform engineer maintaining feature stores
data infrastructure engineer owning Airflow DAGs

non_fit_patterns.label: Pure sales — AE / BDR / account management
non_fit_patterns.description: Carries a quota, runs the commercial cycle, relies on an SE or product specialist for anything technical.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The seat is the technical half of the pair; without Python and model/API work the screen question (benchmark five models on a dataset and write a report) cannot be answered.
examples: enterprise account executive at a SaaS vendor
SDR promoted to AE at a data company
customer success manager with renewal ownership and no code

non_fit_patterns.label: BI / dashboard analyst
non_fit_patterns.description: SQL, Tableau or Looker dashboards, recurring business reporting for internal stakeholders.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Reporting alone misses both the hands-on Python/LLM gate and the customer-facing technical gate; the reports here are produced from model runs the person executed themselves.
examples: marketing analytics analyst building Looker dashboards
financial reporting analyst in Excel and SQL

non_fit_patterns.label: Staff / Principal / Lead IC or people manager
non_fit_patterns.description: Sets technical direction across teams, or manages engineers with reports and hiring responsibility.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: The level gate is junior-to-mid IC; the seat should not pay for seniority it does not need.
examples: staff solutions architect running an enterprise region
head of solutions engineering with a team of six
engineering manager for a platform group

non_fit_patterns.label: Non-technical implementation / support roles
non_fit_patterns.description: Onboarding, configuration, and ticket triage inside a product UI with no code of their own.
non_fit_patterns.why_not: Surface-similar titles (implementation, technical account manager) but the hands-on technical gate fails — no Python, no model APIs, no pipelines.
examples: implementation specialist configuring an HR SaaS tenant
technical support engineer handling tier-2 tickets

employer_signal_rules.evidence_required: The work itself has to be customer-facing and technical — applied, field, forward-deployed, solutions, or partner-engineering work with external labs or customers — plus hands-on Python and model-API work, and a junior-to-mid IC scope. Lab research work is a reject class here regardless of brand.

Look for a seat whose purpose is the technical side of customer work — solutions, forward-deployed, customer, implementation, or client-facing data science — carrying Python and LLM or model-API work at a junior-to-mid IC scope. Time at an AI infrastructure or evaluation-tooling vendor is a strong plus on top of that.

Solutions / sales / customer-engineering titles are common here, so the discriminator is hands-on code and AI exposure: Python, model APIs, LLM or ML/data pipeline work, and a junior-to-mid IC scope rather than a regional or enterprise-lead posture.

Consulting and professional-services histories qualify when the engagement work was technical and client-delivered — Python, LLM or ML/data pipeline build-outs, pilots and POCs the person ran — at a junior-to-mid IC scope rather than pure strategy or project management.

experience_measure: Counts total professional experience, including research and advanced-degree years; the 1–4 band is an advisory level guide read together with titles and scope, and 5+ years weighs against a save without being an automatic reject.
minimum_bar_description: Three hard gates, all on visible or strongly inferable evidence. (1) Customer-facing technical role: the title or the role's purpose is technical customer work — solutions engineer, sales engineer, forward-deployed engineer, customer engineer, implementation engineer, solutions architect, technical account manager, technical consultant, pre-sales, consulting, professional services, or client delivery — or the profile shows substantial client, demo, POC, or pre-sales work. (2) Hands-on technical: writes Python and has worked with LLMs, model APIs, or ML/data pipelines. (3) Individual contributor at a junior-to-mid level, judged from titles and scope with roughly 1–4 years as the guide: Staff, Principal, Lead, and Head-of titles are out, and so are people managers. Evaluation or benchmark experience, startup time, AI-vendor pedigree, school, and publications are not requirements and their absence is never a reject reason.

facial_calibration.yes_rate_rationale: The customer-facing technical title pool in the US is moderately dense and largely readable from snippets, but the junior-to-mid IC ceiling plus the requirement that the technical substance be Python/LLM rather than SaaS configuration removes most of it, so roughly one in five to one in ten snippets should advance.
fast_exit_patterns: Entire history in academia or research labs — PhD, postdoc, research scientist, research engineer, with no commercial customer-facing seat
Entire history in non-technical sales — SDR, BDR, account executive, account manager — with no engineering or data title anywhere
Entire history in recruiting, HR, finance, marketing, or operations functions
Entire history in IT support, helpdesk, field service, or network administration
Entire history in management: engineering manager, director, VP, head-of titles across every position
trajectory_yes_patterns: Solutions engineer, sales engineer, forward-deployed engineer, customer engineer, implementation engineer, or solutions architect title at an AI, ML, data-infrastructure, or developer-tools company, with one to three positions since graduating
Technical consultant or professional-services engineer at an AI or data company, with AI/ML vocabulary in the title or company
Data scientist or AI engineer at an early-stage startup whose profile also carries client, customer, demo, or POC language
Analyst or associate role progressing into an AI-adjacent client-facing engineering title within a few years
Any of the above at an AI infrastructure or model-evaluation tooling vendor
trajectory_ambiguous_patterns: Data scientist at a consultancy or professional-services firm — the snippet does not reveal whether the engagements were client-facing or internal analytics
AI engineer or ML engineer at a seed- or Series-A startup — the snippet shows the code but not whether the person sat in customer conversations
Solutions architect or technical account manager at a large cloud or enterprise-software vendor — the snippet does not reveal whether the work involved Python and model APIs or product configuration
Customer engineer or implementation engineer at a SaaS company outside the AI/data segment — technical depth unknown from the title
Business or product analyst at an AI company — the snippet does not show whether the work was hands-on in Python or reporting-only
trajectory_no_patterns: Every position is a research scientist, research engineer, or academic research role
Every position is backend, infrastructure, platform, or ML engineering inside an internal-facing team with no customer-facing or consulting title anywhere
Every position is quota-carrying sales or account management with no engineering, data, or consulting title
Every position is BI, reporting, or dashboard analytics
Every position carries a Staff, Principal, Lead, Head-of, Director, or manager designation

canonical_broad_patterns: customer-facing technical engineer at an AI company
pre-sales technical resource for a data or ML product
early-career solutions engineer selling to technical buyers
technical arm of a sales team
edge_case_patterns: data scientist whose engagements were delivered directly to external clients
AI engineer at a seed-stage startup who also ran customer demos and pilots
analytics or BI person who pivoted into LLM work and presented results to clients
technical consultant at a boutique AI shop building client pilots in Python
support or implementation engineer at an ML tooling startup who writes code and runs integrations
recent graduate with a startup year spanning delivery, demos, and model benchmarking

example_compounds.boolean: ("solutions engineer" OR "sales engineer" OR "forward deployed engineer" OR "customer engineer" OR "implementation engineer" OR "solutions architect" OR "technical account manager") AND ("LLM" OR "large language model" OR "generative AI" OR "GenAI" OR "machine learning") AND ("Python")
example_compounds.purpose: Title-doorway pass over the canonical pool: customer-facing technical titles ANDed with broad AI vocabulary and a hands-on code anchor, which is exactly the three-gate shape and keeps a US-wide string inside the result cap.

example_compounds.boolean: ("AI consultant" OR "machine learning consultant" OR "data scientist" OR "AI engineer") AND ("proof of concept" OR "POC" OR "pilot deployment") AND ("client-facing" OR "customer-facing" OR "pre-sales" OR "presales") NOT ("research scientist" OR "research engineer" OR "postdoctoral")
example_compounds.purpose: Edge-case probe for the pivoted pool the title pass misses — consultants and client-delivery data scientists who write their own POC and client-facing language — with a NOT clause steering away from the research reject class.

sequencing_heuristics: Open with the title-doorway compound (family A) because all three gates are readable from a customer-facing technical title at an AI or devtools employer; then run the consulting / client-facing data-science probe for the pivoted pool, and only use eval vocabulary to narrow a startup-engineer string, never to lead one.
preflight_confidence_notes: Review most carefully: (1) the level band — the 1–4 year guide and the Staff/Principal/Lead/manager reject class carry the whole leveling decision, and the ceiling is advisory, not a hard gate; (2) the eval/benchmark material is a plus signal and a narrowing term, not the seat's identity or its search vocabulary; (3) employer tiers deliberately omit the three blacklisted names, so lab-alumni weighting is left to the judge's read of the profile.
instructions: THE TARGET: a pre-sales, solutions, or field engineer, the technical person in customer conversations at an AI, ML, data, or developer-tools company. The seat goes by titles such as solutions engineer, sales engineer, forward-deployed engineer, customer engineer, implementation engineer, solutions architect, technical account manager, technical consultant, or a data scientist whose work is client-facing. The level is junior to mid. The sweet spot is roughly 1 to 2 years of professional work, ideally at a startup; 3 to 4 years is acceptable, and a new graduate is possible but not targeted. The person is hands-on enough in Python and with LLM and model APIs to run a benchmark across several models on a dataset and write it up. The seat is closer to a solutions engineer than to a research engineer. It is the technical arm of sales for enterprise engineering customers: the technical voice on sales calls about what the platform can do with their models and data, who also runs a customer's workload on the Babbage platform through its API and reports the numbers, turns results into reports and sales material, keeps the integration guides current, and owns last-mile delivery. The screen: given five models and a dataset, the candidate should know how to benchmark them and write up a report. The identity to search for is customer-facing and technical; eval work is a task the seat does, not the identity to search for.

NOT GATES (never reject for the absence of any of these): frontier-lab or AI-vendor pedigree; school pedigree; research publications; deep evaluation or benchmark-construction experience; years as a count, which is not a hard ceiling — judge the level from titles and scope, with roughly 1 to 4 years as the guide, never from a year count alone.

THE GATES, all three on visible or strongly inferable evidence: (a) CUSTOMER-FACING TECHNICAL ROLE — the title or the role's purpose is customer-facing technical work (solutions engineer, sales engineer, forward-deployed engineer, customer engineer, implementation engineer, solutions architect, technical account manager, technical consultant, consulting, professional services, client delivery, pre-sales), or the profile shows substantial client, demo, proof-of-concept, or pre-sales work. (b) HANDS-ON TECHNICAL — writes Python and has worked with LLMs, model APIs, or ML or data pipelines; evaluation experience is a plus, not the gate. (c) INDIVIDUAL CONTRIBUTOR, JUNIOR TO MID — judged from titles and scope, with roughly 1 to 4 years of professional work as the guide: Staff, Principal, Lead, and Head-of titles are out, and so are people managers.

PLUS SIGNALS, none a gate: (a) EARLY CAREER — roughly 1 to 2 years of professional work, ideally at a startup; (b) LLM OR EVALUATION WORK — running models over datasets, benchmarks, comparisons across models, LLM-as-judge; (c) startup experience — scrappy and willing to put in the work; (d) time at an AI infrastructure or evaluation-tooling vendor (Anyscale, Baseten, Replicate, Arize AI, Humanloop, Braintrust), or at an AI or developer-tools company selling to technical buyers; (e) a San Francisco Bay Area location — the Bay Area ranks first among US locations, and a US location elsewhere is never a reason to reject.

WEIGHED AGAINST, never alone a reject: a current title containing 'Senior', and roughly 5 or more years of professional work. Both point to someone the seat would overpay, so either lowers a profile's priority and counts against a save when the rest of the evidence is close; neither is a reason to reject on its own. Only gate (c) and the Staff, Principal, Lead, and people-manager reject class reject on level.

REJECT CLASSES: research scientists and research engineers, and anyone whose career is research; Staff, Principal, and Lead individual contributors, and people managers; pure backend, infrastructure, platform, or ML engineers with no customer-facing role; pure sales — account executives and business-development people with no hands-on technical work; BI or dashboard analysts with no Python or LLM work.

STRING FORMATION — Boolean-first. Strings OPEN with customer-facing technical TITLES — solutions engineer, sales engineer, forward deployed engineer, customer engineer, implementation engineer, solutions architect, technical account manager, AI consultant, and "pre-sales" or "presales" — ANDed with AI vocabulary kept broad (AI, "machine learning", LLM, "generative AI", GenAI). Three string families, in this priority: (A) customer-facing technical titles at AI, ML, data, and developer-tools companies, where company names are allowed; (B) client-facing data scientists and AI or ML consultants, with consulting and professional-services vocabulary; (C) AI or data engineers at startups whose profiles carry customer, client, demo, or POC vocabulary. Do NOT build strings around benchmark names (SWE-bench, MMLU, HumanEval, GPQA, HELM, BIG-bench, and similar), evaluation-tool names (Ragas, DeepEval, LangSmith, and similar), or evaluation-metric vocabulary (pass@k and similar): eval words may narrow a string in family C and must never lead one. The Location permanent filter ('United States') is the only filter. One Boolean yields at most 625 people, so a US-wide string needs enough narrowing to keep its result count within reach.

Excluded employers (operator ruling 2026-08-07, binding across all modules): candidates CURRENTLY employed at OpenAI or Anthropic are never leads; Babbage is the hiring company and is never sourced. All three ride in employer_blacklist. Alumni of those labs are in scope and are a plus. GENERATION CONSTRAINT (a deterministic lint aborts the run on violation): the names OpenAI, Anthropic, and Babbage must appear ONLY in employer_blacklist — never in any employer_signal_rules tier pattern, in either targeting or exclusionary phrasing ('alumni only', 'ex-OpenAI', 'current is blacklisted' all still name the employer and all fail the lint). Do not create an alumni tier for these labs; the judge weighs lab alumni from the profile.

Evidence posture: a SAVE is a decision to reach out for a conversation, not to hire, and a 'maybe' poisons every 'yes'. Save when all three gates — the customer-facing technical role, hands-on technical work, and the junior-to-mid IC level — are met on visible or strongly inferable evidence; reject otherwise. An inferential save is allowed when the title makes customer-facing technical work the purpose of the seat, for example a solutions engineer or forward-deployed engineer at an AI company whose profile text is thin. Evaluation experience strengthens a save; its absence is never a reason to reject. The level gate is judged from titles and scope, with roughly 1 to 4 years as the guide: early career, ideally at a startup, strengthens a save, and a current Senior title or 5 or more years of professional work weighs against one but is never alone a reason to reject.
